full_judgment: 3. The fact of the plaint of the aforesaid suit, in brief, is that the suit land appertaining to CS khatian No. 18 of Mouza Apusagari, Police Station Nandigram, District-Bogura originally belonged to Bidu Shah, Sobed Ali Shah in four anna share each, Mohiron Nesa and Kabu Bewa two anna share each. Kabu Shah and Sobed Ali Shah and one daughter Mohiron Nesa as the heirs of his two anna shares. Mohiron Nesa died leaving his three brothers Bidu Shah, Hodu Shah and Sobed Ali Shah as her heirs. Hodu Shah died leaving behind his two brothers Bidu Shah and Sobed Ali Shah as his heirs and Sobed Ali Shandied leaving behind his only brother Bidu Shah as his heir. In these way Bidu Shah became owner and possessor of CS Khatian No. 18 and MRR khatian No. 23 was prepared in his name with the land of CS khatian 18 and some other land. Thereafter Bidu Shah died leaving behind his only son Abdul Goni as his heir of the land of Dag No. 99 who died leaving behind his four sons Abdul Gafur, Golam Rabbani(plaintiff), Golam Mostafa, Golam Yasmin and three daughters Rowsan Ara, Motiun Nahar, Asia and a wife Rabeya Bewa as his heirs. Golam Rabbani became the owner and possessor of 1.02 acres of land of Dag No. 99 of Police Station Nandigram, Mouza Apusagari by verbal compromise that the defendant Tania Akter Jemi with the advice of his father and other relatives filed a false case in the court of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Adalat-1, Bogura being Nari-o-Shishu Case No. 55P/07 against the petitioner, his son Rashedul Bari, wife Hena Begum and his full brother Yasin Ali. Thereafter, the opposite party instituted Family Suit No. 797 of 2007 in the Family Court, Bogura against the petitioner and his son for realization of dower and maintenance. The petitioner and his son contested the Family Suit by filing written statement and the statement made in the plaint of the Family Suit is absolutely false and concocted and the father of the opposite party have no financial capacity to give a loan of Taka 3(three) lac to the son of the petitioner. The petitioner is a businessman and financially solvent person and there is no reason of his borrowing money from the father of the opposite party. On perusal of the certified copy of the complaint of Criminal Case No. 55P/2007 and the plaint of Family Suit No. 797 of 2007 the petitioner came to know that the opposite party have collusively get the deed of Heba-bil-Awaz dated 19-7-2006 executed and registered in her name. In fact, the petitioner agreed to transfer the suit land in favour of his son by a deed of Heba-bil-Awaz but the opposite party in convenience with the deed writer has created the deed of Heba-bil-Awaz in her name. The opposite party did not pay any consideration to the petitioner in respect of the alleged deed of Heba-bil-Awaz and the petitioner also did not receive any conside-ration from the opposite party in respect of the alleged deed of Heba-bil-Awaz. The opposite party did not get any possession of the suit land by virtue of the said deed of Heba-bil-Awaz and that the deed of Heba-bil-Awaz is illegal, collusive, null and void without any consideration and not binding upon the plaintiff.
